messages:
maya: Observed a throughput drop after the continuous-batching tweak + streaming flush cadence change. Repro steps below and a short perf dump.

maya: Repro: send 1200 short-chat requests (avg len ~24 tokens) with streaming enabled and token_budget_target=0.6. Baseline (old heuristics) = 11.8k TPS tokens/sec, new = 9.1k. Latency p95 jumped ~35%.

maya: Profiling (hotspots):
```
-- kernel_select: 28% (more nvrtc falls through to generic kernels)
-- batch_formation: 18% (flush thrashing on partial-decode)
-- kv_cache_lock: 12% (memcpy stalls during partial decode eviction)
-- decode_thread_wakeup: 10% (excess wakeups due to tiny flushes)
```

oliver: Hmm. Token budget target + streaming probably causing very small batches to flush early. Did the change to aggressive prefix aging land with the same queue weights? :thinking:

maya: Yes that landed in last PR. We reduced queue_age_penalty from 0.15 -> 0.05 and lowered min_batch_wait_ms for stream routes to 2ms. The idea was faster tail latency but looks like it regresses throughput.

priya: Can you paste the exact route config? I want to run a quick sim in the load harness.

maya: Route config snippet:
```
route: chat-stream
max_batch_tokens: 4096
token_budget_target: 0.6
min_batch_wait_ms: 2
queue_age_penalty: 0.05
partial_decode_enabled: true
```

dan: FWIW I saw KV cache memcpy spikes when partial_decode interleaves with batch formation. Small batches cause frequent KV writes + readbacks -> locks. Likely why kv_cache_lock is 12%.

oliver: Two quick ideas: 1) Prefer kernel routing for stream-enabled requests by bumping selection threshold so we avoid generic kernel path on short sequences. 2) Add a min_batch_token_budget floor for stream routes so we don't flush below X tokens (e.g., 0.3).

priya: Running a quick AB locally: branch with token_budget_floor=0.3 and kernel_threshold bump (+0.1). Will share numbers in ~5m.

infra-bot: Deploy queued: https://deploys/redwood/12345 — test branch: batch-stream-kernel-fix (manual canary scheduled).

maya: Attached a tiny flame snippet for the batch formation phase (textified): high tail on splice_wait + memcpy.

oliver: If splice_wait correlates with tiny flushes, increasing min_batch_wait_ms slightly (2 -> 4 or 6ms) might let small coalescing happen without hurting p95 much. The previous reduction to 2ms is probably too aggressive for our VM load.

priya: AB result (30k requests):
- baseline (old heuristics): tokens/sec = "11800"
- prod (current change): tokens/sec = "9100"
- prod + token_budget_floor=0.3 + kernel_threshold+0.1: tokens/sec = "11250"
- prod + min_batch_wait_ms=6: tokens/sec = "11020"
Latency p95: prod was +35%, both mitigations bring p95 back within ~5% of baseline.

maya: Nice. Any KV cache impact numbers?

priya: kv lock cycles dropped from 12% -> 6% with token_budget_floor. memcpy hotpath reduced. partial_decode still causes some writes but less churn.

dan: That matches observed behavior. The floor prevents the tiny partial-decode-driven flushes that do a bunch of KV churn per-request.

oliver: For kernel selection: we should log the selected kernel variant in prod for a few hours to confirm fewer fallbacks. Add a metric: kernel_variant_chosen and kernel_fallback_count by route. Also emit batch_token_count distribution for stream routes.

maya: I'll add the logging and a short canary. Plan: roll the token_budget_floor=0.3 + kernel_threshold bump to 10% canary on chat-stream for 2h, collect kernel_fallback_count, batch_size_hist, kv_lock_time.

infra-bot: Canary started: https://canary/redwood/streams/67890 (rolling 10%)

oliver: Also consider a micro-heuristic: if partial_decode_enabled && batch_size <=2 then prefer partial_only decode path (avoids heavy KV writes). That should help worst-case tiny-batch behavior.

maya: Good call. We can gate that behind a feature flag and try it in the canary if initial metrics look good.

priya: After 20m of canary: kernel_fallback_count down 72%, batch_size mean +18%, kv_lock_time down 40%. TPS trending +18% compared to prod.

maya: Great. If numbers hold for 2h we can promote. Any regression risks?

dan: Watch cold-starts on large seqs — kernel_threshold bump could cause slower compilation paths if mispredicted. We should only bump threshold for stream routes where seq lengths are shallow. Also add guard: if avg_seq_len > 512 don't apply bump.

oliver: Agree. Implement guard by route using observed seq_len hist. Also add telemetry to monitor kernel compile latency spikes.

sre-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-03-17-1 — perf regression detected and mitigated via canary tweaks.

maya: Thanks everyone. Action items I'll follow up:
- add kernel_variant/logging + batch hist metrics (maya)
- roll token_budget_floor=0.3 + kernel bump -> 10% canary (infra)
- feature-flag partial-only decode for tiny batches (oliver/priya)
- add seq_len guard for kernel bump (dan)

maya: Will post a brief follow-up with the promotion decision in this thread. :rocket:
